purpose: Verify the sample-unit and ego-projection contract in the distributed CooperScene mini indexes, then compare that contract with the fixed official converter without downloading the complete 2.9 GB archive.

extractionIntegrity.pickleSafety: pickletools found no GLOBAL opcode. A custom unpickler rejected every class lookup and accepted only the built-in list, tuple, dictionary, number, string, and boolean payloads present in the three indexes.

verifiedInvariants: Every physical event has exactly four rows and agent IDs 0, 1, 2, and 3 each take the ego role once.
Every projection references the same four event-level LiDAR source paths while changing the ego and cooperator roles.
Every projection has a distinct instance payload after ego-coordinate transformation; the rows are not byte-identical duplicates.
Every released .bin reference has a matching .pcd source member in the archive, while the .bin itself must be generated during documented data preparation.
sample_idx is unique and sequential from zero inside each split.
The three released indexes label metainfo.dataset as OPV2V.

currentConverterContract.readmeEvidence: README lines 68-78 instruct the user to run tools/dataset_converters/coop_data_converter.py and state that it writes the same three index filenames.

codeEvidence.finding: The converter documents three samples per event, with only vehicles 1, 2, and 3 taking the ego role.
The generation loop rejects every ego whose agent ID is not in EGO_CANDIDATE_IDS.
The generated index metainfo labels the dataset as CooperScene.

deterministicSchemaDifference: The distributed mini indexes contain four ego rows per event, including infrastructure agent 0; the fixed converter permits three vehicle ego rows.
The distributed indexes use metainfo.dataset=OPV2V; the fixed converter writes metainfo.dataset=CooperScene.
repositoryHistory: The first public converter commit, 2c91d6c55e782a84871ef63f39d6b2f7720a843b on 2026-05-29, already restricted ego candidates to vehicles 1, 2, and 3 and wrote metainfo.dataset=CooperScene.
Commit ca5eb9049ff2a107a23753e9b50b0a66e7a8a85f on 2026-06-17 fixed rotation, intensity, and cooperative-ground-truth handling without introducing the distributed four-ego contract.

The official manifest dates all three distributed pickle members to 2026-05-22, before the first public converter commit. Their exact historical generator is not present in the public repository history.
currentConverterContract.dynamicRunBoundary: This audit proves a released-index versus fixed-code contract mismatch. It does not claim byte-for-byte regenerated output or attribute either contract to a published result without running the complete fixed pipeline and tracing the result provenance.

paperBenchmarkContract.evidence: Lines 151-154 state that the multi-ego pipeline iteratively treats each of the three vehicles as ego, uses the remaining vehicles and infrastructure as cooperators, and averages results over ego vehicles.
paperBenchmarkContract.comparison: The paper contract agrees with the fixed three-vehicle-ego converter and disagrees with the four-ego distributed mini indexes.
paperBenchmarkContract.attributionBoundary: Protocol agreement does not prove which concrete index artifact, command, or commit produced any published table.

datasetLoader.finding: The public loader defines V+... settings around a vehicle ego and treats agent 0 as infrastructure. An infrastructure-ego release row therefore belongs to a different cohort and cannot silently inherit the vehicle-ego interpretation.

evaluator.finding: The evaluator retains sample_idx and pools detections into global AP. It does not preserve a physical-event key or emit vehicle-versus-infrastructure cohort summaries, so paired event analysis requires a frozen index join and cached per-projection outcomes.

runtimeEvaluationContract.claimBoundary: Static code inspection establishes the available cohort and aggregation fields, not the direction or magnitude of any performance effect.

interpretation: The four rows are legitimate receiver-conditioned projections if both vehicle-centric and infrastructure-centric tasks are in scope.
The four rows share one physical acquisition event and must be treated as a cluster for claims whose sampling unit is the road event.
The released-index and paper/current-converter protocols define different evaluation populations because only the distributed index includes infrastructure ego.

The released pickle members predate the first public converter commit, and the complete public history contains no generator for their four-ego OPV2V contract. The archive also predates the later converter fix. This provenance gap does not resolve which artifact is authoritative.
The mismatch may change aggregate metrics, weighting, uncertainty, and method order, but none of those effects is claimed before fixed predictions are evaluated under both protocols.
No train-validation-test event overlap was observed in the mini indexes.

researchCandidate.workingTitle: Release-regeneration parity and physical-event inference for multi-ego cooperative benchmarks
falsifiableQuestions: Does the fixed official converter reproduce the distributed index contract for every release, split, event, ego role, source path, and annotation payload?
How much of each aggregate result is caused by including infrastructure ego, by row weighting, and by the underlying method rather than by new physical-event evidence?
Do physical-event paired intervals or equal-event-exposure training change a close method comparison relative to row-wise aggregation?
If every result is stable, can the release obtain a bounded protocol-equivalence certificate?
minimumExperiments: Run the fixed converter in an isolated environment on the official mini archive and compare canonical event, ego, path, annotation, and metainfo manifests with the distributed indexes.
Freeze at least two official checkpoints or reproducibly trained baselines and cache per-projection outcomes.
Report vehicle-only, infrastructure-only, four-ego row-weighted, and equal-physical-event-weighted results separately.
Use paired physical-event resampling for method differences and report row-wise resampling only as a deliberately misspecified comparator.
Train one-random-ego, cyclic-ego, vehicle-only-all-ego, and four-ego variants while matching unique event exposures and optimizer steps in separate controlled analyses.
researchCandidate.positiveResult: A protocol choice changes an inference, ranking, or deployment conclusion under a preregistered materiality margin and is reproduced from a fixed release manifest.
researchCandidate.negativeResult: All primary comparisons remain within the preregistered equivalence margin, yielding a useful release-parity and statistical-robustness certificate.
killCriteria: No fixed checkpoint, reproducible baseline, or cached prediction can support paired outcome analysis.
The full release does not preserve a stable physical-event and ego-projection manifest.

A primary paper already publishes the same release-versus-regeneration manifest, infrastructure-ego decomposition, physical-event paired inference, and equal-exposure training ablation for CooperScene.

claimGuardrails: Do not call the four ego projections duplicate acquisitions.
Do not call the protocol mismatch train-test leakage.
Do not claim metric inflation, narrower intervals, ranking changes, or benchmark invalidity before paired outcomes are computed.
Do not infer which index contract produced a paper table without command, artifact, and checkpoint provenance.
Do not generalize from the 180-frame mini smoke-test subset to the full release or a deployment population.
Do not treat regenerated source-code output as authoritative without recording the exact commit and environment.
